q: what is the deepest point in the ocean
where is the deepest point in the ocean
what lives in the deepest ocean
a: The deepest point in the ocean is the Challenger Deep, located at the southern end of the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean, near Guam. Its depth is approximately 10,994 meters (36,070 feet) below sea level. To put that in perspective, Mount Everest would fit inside with over 2 kilometers of water above it. The Mariana Trench was formed by the subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath the Mariana Plate. Despite the extreme pressure (over 1,000 times atmospheric pressure), complete darkness, and near-freezing temperatures, life exists at these depths. Creatures adapted to this environment include amphipods (small shrimp-like crustaceans), holothurians (sea cucumbers), xenophyophores (giant single-celled organisms), and various microorganisms. Other notable deep points include the Tonga Trench (10,882 m), the Philippine Trench (10,540 m), and the Kuril-Kamchatka Trench (10,542 m). Only a handful of manned descents have been made to Challenger Deep: the Trieste bathyscaphe in 1960 (Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh), filmmaker James Cameron in 2012 in the Deepsea Challenger, and Victor Vescovo in 2019 in the DSV Limiting Factor. Recent expeditions have discovered new species including the Mariana snailfish and various microbial life forms.
